First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,{{5{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}-4\sqrt{2}{x}_{1}+4\sqrt{2}{x}_{2}=8
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}-4\sqrt{2}{x}_{1}+4\sqrt{2}{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}-4\sqrt{2}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2})+4\sqrt{2}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2}) & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}+8{y}_{2} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{2}^{2}+8{y}_{2} & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4({y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{2}) & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4({y}_{2}^{2}+2{y}_{2}+1-1) & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4{({y}_{2}+1)}^{2}-4 & =8 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+4{({y}_{2}+1)}^{2} & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables

$$
{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1}={y}_{1}, \\ {z}_{2}={y}_{2}+1,\end{aligned}
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{z}_{1}^{2}+4{z}_{2}^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{z}_{2}^{2}}{3} & =1 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{{z}_{2}^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This represents an ellipse with semiaxes $\sqrt{2}$ and $\sqrt{3}.$

{z1=y1,z2=y2+1,
